subject: URGENT: StormGate AZ3 surge — request to initiate cross-region routing
messages:
From: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@stormgate.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: High 5xx rate + 600ms p95 from our AZ3 customers

Kimberly —

We started seeing a spike around 07:45 PDT: p95 tail latency up to ~600ms and a sustained 5xx rate (~2.3%). Affected endpoints are /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings; roughly 18% of our requests over the past 25 minutes. We've attached a short log sample. This is impacting checkout personalization on our web tier.

We've already scaled our side and retried, but client-side retries are making the error amplification worse. Can Redwood confirm if anything shows up on your side for AZ3 (us-west-2a) and whether you have a recommended immediate mitigation (traffic steering / fallback)?

Attaching: stormgate_error_sample.log (attached)

—Daniel
Director of Platform Ops, StormGate
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: High 5xx rate + 600ms p95 from our AZ3 customers

Forwarding StormGate report — they attached a short log sample. Initial ask: urgent mitigation and whether we can route their traffic to us-west-2b or us-east-1 while we contain the AZ3 issue.

Quick context: StormGate is in expansion; they've been hitting our AZ3 capacity earlier this week. They are hitting checkout flows (high QPS) and will escalate to their CTO if we don't get ahead of this.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi / Hannah: confirm if AZ3 (cluster-w3) shows elevated host error rate + KV cache thrash. Any chance to reduce token-processing latency without full failover?
- Vanessa / Aditya / Marissa: please prepare a short exec note for StormGate and confirm process for initiating a cross-region route (we need approval for priority pin + temporary geo-steer).

[attachment: stormgate_error_sample.log (text/plain)]

—Kimberly
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High 5xx rate + 600ms p95 from our AZ3 customers

Kimberly — quick triage from infra:
- Observed: a narrow host group in us-west-2a (AZ3) showing increased token-gen latencies and transient NVMe stalls on two nodes; autoscaler kept adding pods but KV cache warmup caused amplification. 5xxs correlate with the same host set.
- Impact window: began ~07:40 PDT and still active.
- Risk: If we immediately redirect traffic, cold-cache penalty could temporarily increase latency for heavy sessions; however, keeping traffic into unhealthy AZ will keep error rates high.

Recommended immediate path (0–30 min):
1) Divert 30% of StormGate traffic to us-west-2b (same region but different AZ) and monitor error rate for 10m. This reduces immediate 5xx exposure and limits eviction churn.
2) If errors fall <0.5% and p95 drops ~50–100ms, continue ramp to 100% over 20 minutes.
3) If diversion fails, initiate cross-region fallback to us-east-1 with priority pin (requires ops approval).

I've prepared a short routing playbook (proposed_routing_playbook.pdf) with the step commands and rollback thresholds.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High 5xx rate + 600ms p95 from our AZ3 customers

Rishi's numbers align with what I'm seeing in the console traces. Added notes:
- There are ~12 long-lived sessions at StormGate that keep KVC entries hot on AZ3 hosts; those sessions will experience a small cold-cache cost if we move them.
- No alerts on infra that indicate underlying network fabric issue, points to local NVMe I/O contention.

I support Rishi's diversion plan. I'll coordinate the observability hooks and add a dashboard for the StormGate route so customer success and execs can watch live metrics.

—Hannah
Sr. Reliability Engineer
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: ACTION: approval needed to enact geo-steer for StormGate (AZ3)

Marissa / Aditya —

We need a quick approval to start a conservative geo-steer for StormGate traffic (30% to us-west-2b) per Rishi's playbook. Business impact: StormGate is a mid-enterprise account on an expansion contract; they are currently experiencing checkout errors that hit revenue metrics. Customer is already elevated to their CTO.

Ask: approve temporary priority pin and cross-AZ diversion. We'll route only StormGate's customer token prefix and keep other customers on normal routing. If approved I will:
- Trigger diversion (30%) now, monitor for 10m
- Share live dashboard with StormGate and internal execs
- Escalate to cross-region fallback only if the AZ3 diversion does not reduce 5xx below 0.5% in 20m

Approval options (reply-all):
- APPROVE: proceed with AZ diversion now
- APPROVE+FALLBACK: proceed AZ diversion, pre-authorize cross-region fallback if threshold not met within 20m
- DENY: we do not route — continue to contain within AZ

—Vanessa
Director, Commercial Ops
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@stormgate.com>, ops@stormgate.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: URGENT: StormGate AZ3 surge — request to initiate cross-region routing

Daniel — quick update and proposed immediate action: we recommend starting a conservative AZ diversion (30% to us-west-2b) now; if that reduces your 5xxs below 0.5% within 10–20 minutes we'll ramp to 100% and keep full traffic in-region. If it does not, with your permission we will failover to us-east-1 as a last-resort fallback.

We plan to:
- Trigger 30% diversion at 08:05 PDT (now)
- Monitor error rate and p95; share live dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.com/streams/stormgate-surge
- Keep you posted every 10 minutes with a short status update

Please reply to confirm you accept the temporary diversion and the possible cross-region fallback.

[attachment: proposed_routing_playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

—Kimberly
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: URGENT: StormGate AZ3 surge — request to initiate cross-region routing

Kimberly — confirmed. Please proceed with the AZ diversion now. We prefer regional (us-west-2b) over cross-region if it resolves the issue. Keep us posted on the 10-minute cadence.

Thanks for the quick response — Elena is on standby.

—Daniel
